review_status: Evidence reviewed 2026-11-17. NOAA and WDFW sources support deep adult habitat and diel vertical migration; tagged fish temperature is not satellite SST.

profile.size: Min limit None / Bag limit 2-5 per harvester / day

profile.behavior: Navigates West Coast kelp forests, rocky reefs, and coastal upwelling zones.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred Pacific temperature range for sablefish.
factors.value_notes: NOAA archival tags found sablefish typically at 3.9-5.0 °C (median 4.4 °C), with seasonal temperature variation during diel vertical migration. These are ambient temperatures at the fish's depth, not satellite SST. Adults are deepwater and juveniles occupy near-surface waters, so the configured 4-12 °C SST range and 6-10 °C ideal are not validated by the reviewed evidence; keep values unchanged and mark needs_source.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, within prime Pacific depth zone for sablefish.
factors.value_notes: NOAA and WDFW describe adults on mud bottoms at roughly 200-1,500 m, while juveniles occupy the water column and nearshore nurseries. Adult tags recorded fish depths typically 326-553 m (median 446 m), with a 12-1,621 m range and diel vertical migration. The configured 100-500 m range overlaps the adult core but misses much deeper adult habitat and juvenile pelagic habitat; tagged fish depth is not identical to seabed depth.
